issues.legal_issue: A puisne mortgagee may bring a separate suit on its mortgage when the prior mortgagee has been paid before the mortgaged property is sold in the prior mortgage suit.
material_facts: The puisne mortgagee was joined as a defendant in the first mortgagee’s suit, in which a preliminary decree and a final decree for sale were passed.
The mortgagor paid the first mortgagee’s decretal amount before the property was sold, and no sale took place.
The puisne mortgagee later brought a separate suit on its own mortgage.
issues.conclusion: The puisne mortgagee was entitled to bring a separate suit on its mortgage. Its participation in the prior suit did not entitle it to insist on a sale or to obtain a personal decree when the first mortgagee had been paid before sale.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Transfer of Property Act and Order 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a puisne mortgagee is joined in a prior mortgagee’s suit to allow it to redeem the prior mortgage and to claim any surplus sale proceeds after satisfaction of the prior mortgage. The decree is not, in substance, a decree in the puisne mortgagee’s favour; if no sale occurs because the prior mortgage is paid, the puisne mortgagee may sue separately. The Court approved Chandra Roy Chowdhry v. M. M. Nahapiet, Vedavyasa Ayyar v. The Madura Hindu Labha Nidhi Co. Ltd., and Shiv Kumar Prosad v. The Trustees for the Improvement of Calcutta.

rule.if: prior_mortgage_suit and puisne_mortgagee_joined_in_prior_suit and prior_mortgage_paid_before_sale and no_sale_occurred

predicates.prior_mortgage_suit: A mortgagee holding an earlier mortgage brought a suit to enforce that mortgage.
predicates.puisne_mortgagee_joined_in_prior_suit: A mortgagee holding a later mortgage was made a party to the earlier mortgagee’s suit.
predicates.prior_mortgage_paid_before_sale: The mortgagor paid the earlier mortgagee’s decretal amount before the mortgaged property was sold.
predicates.no_sale_occurred: The mortgaged property was not sold in the earlier suit.
predicates.puisne_mortgagee_may_bring_separate_mort: The later mortgagee is entitled to bring a separate suit to enforce its mortgage.

issues.definition: When a later mortgagee was joined in an earlier mortgage suit but the earlier mortgage was paid before any sale, the later mortgagee may bring a separate suit on its mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: A court has discretion to award post-suit interest on a mortgage at a reasonable rate rather than at the contractual rate.
material_facts: The mortgage provided for interest at 12 percent per annum with monthly rests.
The High Court allowed interest at the contractual rate after the suit was filed.
The Supreme Court considered the post-suit interest and found simple interest at 6 percent per annum on the principal sum adjudged appropriate until redemption.
issues.conclusion: The contractual rate was not required to apply after the suit was filed. In the circumstances, simple interest at 6 percent per annum on the principal sum adjudged was appropriate from the suit date through the date of redemption.
issues.legal_principle: Order 34, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, inserted by the 1929 amendment, provides that the court may order interest up to the payment date at the rate payable on the principal and gives the court discretion over pendente lite and subsequent interest. Applying Jaigobind Singh v. Lachmi Narain Ram, the Court held that contractual interest is not invariably obligatory after suit, even if the rate is not penal, excessive, or substantially unfair under the Usurious Loans Act, 1918. The Court distinguished the earlier position under section 34 and the pre-amendment mortgage rules.

predicates.mortgage_suit: A proceeding was brought to enforce a mortgage.
predicates.post_suit_interest_at_issue: The amount or rate of interest after commencement of the suit was disputed or required determination.
predicates.mortgage_contract_sets_interest_rate: The mortgage agreement specified a rate of interest on the principal.
predicates.court_may_award_post_suit_interest_at_a_: The court may determine post-suit interest at a rate it considers reasonable rather than necessarily applying the contractual rate.

issues.definition: In a mortgage suit where post-suit interest is at issue and the mortgage sets an interest rate, the court may award post-suit interest at a reasonable rate.
